text: Dental caries is the progressive destruction of tooth enamel caused by acids produced by bacteria in dental plaque.
Dental caries commonly develops due to frequent sugar intake, poor oral hygiene, and prolonged plaque accumulation.
Maintaining good oral hygiene, reducing sugary foods, and regular dental checkups can help prevent dental caries.
Until a dental visit, brushing gently, flossing carefully, and avoiding sugary snacks may help reduce discomfort.
Dental calculus is hardened dental plaque that forms on teeth when plaque is not removed regularly. It provides a rough surface that allows more plaque to accumulate.
Calculus develops when dental plaque is left on teeth for long periods and becomes mineralized by saliva. Poor oral hygiene and irregular dental cleaning contribute to its formation.

source: Odell's Clinical Problem Solving in Dentistry
text: Regular tooth brushing, flossing, and routine professional dental cleanings help prevent calculus buildup.
Maintaining good oral hygiene and attending regular dental visits can reduce further buildup until professional cleaning is performed.
Gingivitis is a mild form of gum disease characterized by inflammation, redness, and bleeding of the gums.
Gingivitis is commonly caused by plaque buildup along the gum line due to inadequate oral hygiene.
Brushing twice daily, flossing, and regular dental checkups help prevent gingivitis.
Gentle brushing and maintaining clean gums may reduce discomfort until professional care is received.
A mouth ulcer is a small painful sore that develops inside the mouth, often on the cheeks, lips, or tongue.
Mouth ulcers can result from minor injuries, stress, or irritation from sharp teeth or dental appliances.
Avoiding mouth trauma and maintaining good oral hygiene can help reduce the risk of ulcers.
Avoiding spicy or acidic foods and keeping the mouth clean may help reduce discomfort.
Tooth discoloration refers to changes in the natural color of teeth, appearing yellow, brown, or stained.
Discoloration can be caused by food and drinks, smoking, or natural aging of teeth.
Limiting staining foods and maintaining proper oral hygiene can help prevent discoloration.
Regular brushing and avoiding known staining substances may help reduce visible discoloration.
Hypodontia is a condition where one or more teeth fail to develop naturally.
Hypodontia is usually genetic and occurs during tooth development.
There is no prevention for hypodontia, but early dental assessment helps manage the condition.
Regular dental follow-ups help monitor oral development and maintain oral health.
Dental plaque is a sticky film of bacteria that forms on teeth and gums.
Plaque forms when bacteria in the mouth feed on sugars and starches from food.
Daily brushing and flossing help prevent plaque accumulation.
Keeping teeth clean helps reduce plaque buildup until a dental visit.
Halitosis is persistent bad breath that does not improve with normal oral hygiene.
It may be caused by poor oral hygiene, plaque buildup, or dry mouth.
Regular brushing, flossing, and hydration help reduce bad breath.
Maintaining oral cleanliness and drinking water may help manage symptoms.
Tooth sensitivity is discomfort or pain when teeth are exposed to hot, cold, or sweet substances.
Sensitivity may occur due to enamel wear or exposed tooth surfaces.
Good oral hygiene and avoiding excessive pressure while brushing can help prevent sensitivity.
Avoiding extreme temperatures in food may reduce discomfort temporarily.
Bruxism is the involuntary grinding or clenching of teeth, often during sleep.
It is commonly associated with stress or abnormal bite alignment.
Stress management and regular dental checkups may help reduce bruxism risk.
Being aware of jaw tension and practicing relaxation may reduce discomfort.
